headline: Recognized ChainSecurity audit (Oct 2024) with zero open findings, but no public source repo discovered, Tron bytecode verification unconfirmable, and audit is ~19 months old at analysis date
short_headline: Audited but repo missing, Tron unverifiable

findings.text: Tron is not an EVM chain supported by DeFiPunkd's read API (supported chainIds are Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, etc.). The TRON block explorer (tronscan.org) returned a permission-denied error during this run. Bytecode verification status for all four core contracts (TronUSDCBridge, TronUSDCBridgeController, USDC, USDCController) on Tron cannot be confirmed. The Ethereum-side contracts (TronUSDCBridge, TronUSDCBridgeController) are deployed via TransparentUpgradeableProxy per the audit, but no Ethereum addresses were discoverable from accessible sources in this run to check verification there either.

No public GitHub repository was found for JustCrypto's contract source code. The protocol.github field is empty. A search for 'JustCryptos JUST network bridge audit GitHub smart contract Tron' returned no JustCrypto-specific GitHub repository. The ChainSecurity audit PDF references an internal 'Tron-peg USD Coin repository' without linking it publicly. Without a discoverable public repo, source-to-deployment correspondence cannot be assessed.

ChainSecurity audited the Tron-peg USD Coin (USDC) contracts for JustCrypto. The audit is dated October 21, 2024 and covers three code versions: initial (commit 516b1ab54cc3f2ecde00f6344abbe2836a004a86, Sept 23 2024), fixes (commit 10bee57384cbc7ccf1b30cf0a4ea051af3be0bf5, Oct 8 2024), and pools-on-Ethereum (commit 9a0396111af3a7ea3d0f9b3665cb408481868592, Oct 14 2024). Scope covers TronUSDCBridge.sol, TronUSDCBridgeController.sol, USDC.sol, USDCController.sol, AddressValidator.sol, and TransactionValidator.sol — the core fund-custody and bridging contracts. The audit report was publicly published by ChainSecurity. At analysis date of 2026-05-07, the audit is approximately 19 months old, exceeding the 6-month threshold. No follow-up or re-audit was discovered.

The auditor is ChainSecurity (Decentralized Security AG, Zürich, Switzerland), a recognized firm in the Solidity smart contract security space. Zero critical, high, or medium findings were identified; all 6 low-severity findings were resolved. Three informational findings were acknowledged or resolved.

Post-audit drift cannot be assessed because no public source repository was discoverable. The audit covers commit 9a0396111af3a7ea3d0f9b3665cb408481868592 as the final reviewed version. Without a public repo, any commits added since October 2024 are unknown. Given the ~19-month gap, drift is plausible but unverifiable — recorded as unknown.

The ChainSecurity audit confirms all four core contracts are deployed using OpenZeppelin's TransparentUpgradeableProxy pattern. Separately verifying the proxy contract and its current implementation on Tron is not possible in this run (tronscan.org inaccessible; Tron not supported by DeFiPunkd API). For the Ethereum-side contracts, no deployed addresses were discovered.

steelman.red: No public source repository exists for the JustCrypto contracts, and bytecode verification on Tron cannot be confirmed — an outsider cannot independently verify what the deployed code does without a discoverable public repo or accessible block explorer.
steelman.orange: A recognized firm (ChainSecurity) published a public audit with zero open findings covering all core fund-custody contracts, but the audit is ~19 months old exceeding the 6-month freshness threshold, no public source repo was discoverable, and Tron bytecode verification is unconfirmable — leaving meaningful verification gaps.
steelman.green: ChainSecurity is a broadly recognized Solidity auditor, the published report covers all in-scope contracts, all issues were resolved, and the contracts use standard OpenZeppelin upgradeable patterns, which are themselves well-audited.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because the ChainSecurity audit from a recognized firm with zero open findings is a genuine positive signal, but three conditions prevent green: (1) no public source repository was discovered in this run, making V2 source-to-repo correspondence unassessable; (2) Tron bytecode verification is unconfirmable due to tronscan.org being inaccessible and Tron being unsupported by the DeFiPunkd read API, preventing V1 and V6 checks; (3) the audit is ~19 months old at analysis date without a discoverable follow-up or re-audit, exceeding the 6-month freshness threshold for a green grade. Red is rejected because a recognized-firm audit with zero open findings and a publicly published report provides real verification signal beyond 'no audit / no repo' — the orange grade better reflects the partial-but-incomplete verification posture.

evidence.shows: ChainSecurity's public audit page for JustCrypto's Tron-peg USD Coin (USDC) bridge, confirming the audit was performed, the auditor is ChainSecurity (recognized firm), and a PDF report is available

Full 24-page audit report dated October 21, 2024; scope covers TronUSDCBridge.sol, TronUSDCBridgeController.sol, USDC.sol, USDCController.sol, AddressValidator.sol, TransactionValidator.sol at final commit 9a0396111af3a7ea3d0f9b3665cb408481868592 (Oct 14 2024); all four contracts deployed via OpenZeppelin TransparentUpgradeableProxy; 0 critical/high/medium findings; all 6 low-severity findings resolved; centralization of system noted as very high

unknowns: V1: Tron bytecode verification status for TronUSDCBridge, TronUSDCBridgeController, USDC, USDCController could not be checked — tronscan.org returned permission-denied, and Tron is not a supported chainId on DeFiPunkd's read API; no Ethereum contract addresses discoverable to check Ethereum-side verification
V2: No public GitHub repository found for JustCrypto contract source code; source-to-deployment correspondence unassessable
V5: Post-audit drift unassessable — no public repo means changes since Oct 2024 commit 9a0396111af3a7ea3d0f9b3665cb408481868592 are unknown; ~19-month gap is material
V6: Proxy implementation verification on Tron unconfirmable — tronscan.org inaccessible; Ethereum implementation contract addresses not discovered

protocol_metadata.about: JustCryptos is a bridge protocol that connects the TRON network with Ethereum, allowing users to transfer USDC between the two chains. Users lock USDC in a TronUSDCBridge escrow contract on Ethereum, and an operator mints an equivalent Tron-peg USDC token on Tron via a tiered ratification system (instant, ratified, multi-sig). The reverse direction burns Tron-USDC and releases native USDC on Ethereum. All core contracts are deployed behind OpenZeppelin TransparentUpgradeableProxy and are highly centralized, with admins holding full control over funds.
